overview: Sigma 4.11's FastLadder is a two-branch ladder-speed override: it listens for EventLadder and, on the pre phase, replaces the vanilla climb velocity with the MOTION setting value via el.setMotionY(). Vanilla 1.8 caps ladder ascent at 0.15 blocks per tick; the setting ships at 1.0 (increment 0.005, range 0.2-1.0), so the default climbs roughly 6.7 times faster than vanilla. There is no packet logic in the module itself - it only changes the motionY value the movement hook bakes into the next C03PacketPlayer - which makes it a pure per-move vertical speed hack that content-aware movement envelopes are designed to catch.

sections.p: The module registers a single handler for EventLadder and branches on el.isPre(). EventLadder is fired from EntityLivingBase's ladder movement code in two phases: pre carries the vanilla-computed motionY and lets listeners replace it before the client applies the climb, post fires after. Only the pre write matters here - setMotionY overwrites the value that becomes the player's vertical velocity for that tick, and because ladder climbing in 1.8 applies motionY directly (0.15 while holding up on a ladder), the setting value is what the server measures as the per-tick ascent. The motion range of 0.2-1.0 means even the minimum setting exceeds vanilla's 0.15.

The single MOTION setting is constructed as Setting<>(MOTION, 1, "FastLadder motion.", 0.005, 0.2, 1) - the five-argument constructor takes (name, value, description, increment, min, max), so the default is 1.0 with a 0.2-1.0 slider in 0.005 steps. At the default the player teleports upward one full block per tick while climbing, which is faster than any vanilla mechanism (jump ascent peaks near 0.42 for one tick, ladder ascent is 0.15 sustained). The module has no onEnable/onDisable logic and no state, so it is always on the moment it is enabled and applies to any climbable surface the client reports, including vines.

files.label: FastLadder.java (module)
files.explanation: The entire module is the constructor (which seeds the MOTION setting) and the pre-phase rewrite. The handler pattern is the same as DepthStrider: a @RegisterEvent(events = {EventLadder.class}) method that type-checks the event and mutates one value. Because the module writes motionY from the setting on every ladder tick, the client-side climb velocity is constant at the configured rate instead of vanilla's 0.15, and every C03PacketPlayer during the climb reports a vertical delta equal to that rate. The post phase is ignored, so no listener can undo the rewrite after the fact. There are no packets constructed here and no timer, which is why the module is trivially small and why its detection depends entirely on server-side reconstruction of the climb envelope.

files.label: EventLadder.java (motion carrier)
files.explanation: EventLadder is the carrier: fire(double motionY, boolean pre) is called from EntityLivingBase's ladder handling with the current climb velocity, and setMotionY replaces it. The pre/post flag is what lets the client distinguish the writable phase (pre) from the notification phase (post); the file's comment 'Dans entitylivingbase' marks where the vanilla hook lives. The double motionY field is exactly what becomes the vertical velocity for the tick, so a pre-phase override is sufficient to control the entire climb with no other state.

countering.label: Flight (FastLadder branch)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Flight check contains a dedicated ladder-speed branch. In runBlockChecks it gathers isAscending, isClimbing and the air/ladder tick counters, and only evaluates the climb when actuallyInAir (airTicks >= 20 and ladderTime >= 8) so short ground-to-ladder hops do not false-flag. The fast-ladder test fires when isAscending && isClimbing && actuallyInAir and vertical > maxAscendSpeed, where maxAscendSpeed comes from the ascend-ladder config value (default 0.1176000022889); it flags as 'Flight (FastLadder)' with a set-back to the previous location. A second patch catches instant-ladder clients: when vertical - maxAscendSpeed > 1.0 it flags 'ladder_instant' regardless of the sustained-climb guard. Sigma's default motionY of 1.0 exceeds 0.1176 by ~0.88 per tick, so the first sustained climb is flagged and the player is snapped back every tick; even the minimum 0.2 setting sits 0.08 above the ceiling. The set-back target (data.getPreviousLocation()) is re-checked on the next move, so the module cannot outrun the enforcement by climbing faster than the check can rubber-band.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (climbable envelope)
countering.explanation: NCP's vertical envelope clamps ladder motion explicitly. In the yDistanceBeforeCollide computation, when !from.isInLiquid() && from.isOnClimbable() && from.canClimbUp(...) the allowed descent is clamped with yDistanceBeforeCollide = Math.max(yDistanceBeforeCollide, -Magic.CLIMBABLE_MAX_SPEED), where CLIMBABLE_MAX_SPEED is 0.15f - the vanilla climb rate. The horizontal allowance is clamped the same way for climbable blocks in both the input reconstruction and the theoretical-speed pass (thisMove.xAllowedDistance/zAllowedDistance and xTheoreticalDistance[i]/zTheoreticalDistance[i] all clamped to +-CLIMBABLE_MAX_SPEED). A climb reporting 1.0 blocks of vertical motion in one tick therefore presents yDistanceAboveLimit of roughly 0.85, which scores 85 against the per-move multiplier and fires the SurvivalFly violation and set-back on the first ladder tick. Because the clamp is applied to the allowed distance rather than the reported one, the module's setting value only determines how far above the 0.15 ceiling each flag is.

countering.label: Fly (climbable exemption - the gap in this version)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Fly check is the one vertical-speed check that explicitly does NOT cover ladders in this snapshot. Its air branch is gated by !isInClimbable(from.toLocation(pp.getWorld())), where isInClimbable returns true for LADDER and VINE blocks, and the source carries the developer's own TODO: 'uh oh! make sure to have a fastladder check, otherwise hackers can "pop" off them'. The consequence is that a player whose climb keeps their position inside a ladder block never enters the vertical prediction loop, so Sigma's 1.0-blocks-per-tick ascent produces no vertical discrepancy and Fly stays silent for the whole climb. The check only becomes relevant at the moment the module's climb ends (the 'pop' the TODO warns about): the player leaves the ladder block with a motionY of 1.0 and the air branch then sees a large Y jump against a gravity model, which flags as a Fly violation. On a long ladder the module still trips Arc's FastLadder branch and NCP's climbable envelope, but against Hawk alone a sustained ladder climb is undetected - the documented gap in this version.

countering.label: FastLadderProtocol (direct climb-rate detector)
countering.explanation: Negativity ships a purpose-built FastLadder check. On every NegativityPlayerMoveEvent it requires survival/adventure mode, an active detection, no elytra and no flying, then tests the block at the player's feet: the player must be standing on LADDER for two consecutive moves (the isOnLadders latch), must have more than two ladder blocks below (the nbLadder loop), a ladder above (loc.add(0,1,0)), no water around, and no high-level speed potion. The actual test is a single distance check: if the move distance is > 0.23 and < 3.8 the check alerts with a confidence of distance * 350 percent and, when set-back is enabled, snaps the player to the midpoint between the two positions (e.getFrom().clone().add(fl.getX()/2, fl.getY()/2 + 0.5, fl.getZ())). Sigma's default 1.0-block climb is four times the 0.23 threshold and flags on the first sustained move; the 0.2 minimum setting stays just under 0.23 and passes this particular check, though it still fails Arc and NCP. The 0.23-3.8 window is what makes the check ladder-specific - a legitimate jump off a ladder can exceed it, but a sustained 1.0 climb cannot.
